notes.title: PostgreSQL Troubleshooting Runbook
notes.content:
# PostgreSQL Troubleshooting Runbook

Comprehensive guide for PostgreSQL database administration and troubleshooting.

---

## 1. Server Down

### Check Database Status
```bash
ps -ef | grep -i postgres | grep data
ls -a
. .dbname
psql / psql -U dbadmin
```

### Verify Database Uptime
```sql
SELECT date_trunc('second', current_timestamp - pg_postmaster_start_time()) AS db_uptime;
SHOW port;
\! date;
hostname -f;
```

> **Note:** If nothing shows, the database is down.

### Check Logs
```bash
cd $PGDATA/log
ls -a
less <logfilename>  # Choose the last log recorded
```

- Check database activity & connection graphic on PEM
- Take snapshots and inform the apps team

---

## 2. Agent Down

### Check PEM Agent Status
```bash
ps -ef | grep -i pem
systemctl status pemagent
date; hostname -f
```

### Restart PEM Agent
```bash
systemctl start pemagent
```

### Verify Agent is Running
```bash
ps -ef | grep -i pem
systemctl status pemagent
date; hostname -f
```

---

## 3. Total Connections as Percentage of max_connections

### Check Connection Count
```bash
ps -ef | grep -i postgres | grep data
ls -a
. .dbname
psql / psql -U dbadmin
```

```sql
SELECT count(*) FROM pg_stat_activity;
SHOW max_connections;
SHOW port;
\! date;
hostname -f;
```

> If active connections > max_connections, check connection graphic on PEM for last 2 days and analyze spike anomalies.

---

## 4. Number of WAL Files

### Check WAL Files
```bash
ps -ef | grep -i postgres | grep data
ls -a
. .dbname
cd $PGDATA/pg_wal
ll | wc -l
psql / psql -U dbadmin
```

```sql
SHOW wal_keep_segments;
SHOW port;
\! date;
hostname -f;
```

> If WAL files exceed capacity, perform housekeeping by deleting older WAL files (keep only current month).

---

## 5. Dead Tuple Percentage

### Check Dead Tuples
```bash
ps -ef | grep -i postgres | grep data
ls -a
. .dbname
psql / psql -U dbadmin
```

### Show Schema & Connect
```sql
SHOW search_path;
\l+
\dn
SET search_path TO myschema;
```

### Query Dead Tuples
```sql
SELECT relname, schemaname, n_live_tup, n_dead_tup, last_vacuum, last_autovacuum
FROM pg_stat_user_tables
ORDER BY n_dead_tup DESC
LIMIT 10;

SELECT schemaname, relname, n_live_tup, n_dead_tup, last_vacuum, last_autovacuum
FROM pg_stat_all_tables
WHERE n_dead_tup >= 200000
ORDER BY n_dead_tup DESC;
```

### Check Autovacuum Settings
```sql
SHOW autovacuum_vacuum_scale_factor;
SHOW autovacuum_vacuum_threshold;
SHOW autovacuum_analyze_scale_factor;
SHOW autovacuum_analyze_threshold;
```

### Check Autovacuum Running
```sql
SELECT * FROM pg_stat_activity
WHERE query LIKE '%autovacuum%'
AND backend_type = 'autovacuum worker';
```

### Vacuum Commands
- `VACUUM` - Won't change disk space, but new data can be inserted into empty space
- `VACUUM FULL` - Changes disk space, but blocks all operations including SELECT

---

## 6. Number of Ungranted Locks / Query Locking

### Connect to Database
```bash
ps -ef | grep -i postgres | grep data
ls -a
. .dbname
psql / psql -U dbadmin
\l+
\c <database_name>
```

### Check Blocked Queries
```sql
SELECT
    blocked_locks.pid AS blocked_pid,
    blocked_activity.usename AS blocked_user,
    blocking_locks.pid AS blocking_pid,
    blocking_activity.usename AS blocking_user,
    blocked_activity.query AS blocked_statement,
    blocking_activity.query AS current_statement_in_blocking_process,
    blocked_activity.application_name AS blocked_application,
    blocking_activity.application_name AS blocking_application
FROM pg_catalog.pg_locks blocked_locks
JOIN pg_catalog.pg_stat_activity blocked_activity ON blocked_activity.pid = blocked_locks.pid
JOIN pg_catalog.pg_locks blocking_locks
    ON blocking_locks.locktype = blocked_locks.locktype
    AND blocking_locks.DATABASE IS NOT DISTINCT FROM blocked_locks.DATABASE
    AND blocking_locks.relation IS NOT DISTINCT FROM blocked_locks.relation
    AND blocking_locks.page IS NOT DISTINCT FROM blocked_locks.page
    AND blocking_locks.tuple IS NOT DISTINCT FROM blocked_locks.tuple
    AND blocking_locks.virtualxid IS NOT DISTINCT FROM blocked_locks.virtualxid
    AND blocking_locks.transactionid IS NOT DISTINCT FROM blocked_locks.transactionid
    AND blocking_locks.classid IS NOT DISTINCT FROM blocked_locks.classid
    AND blocking_locks.objid IS NOT DISTINCT FROM blocked_locks.objid
    AND blocking_locks.objsubid IS NOT DISTINCT FROM blocked_locks.objsubid
    AND blocking_locks.pid != blocked_locks.pid
JOIN pg_catalog.pg_stat_activity blocking_activity ON blocking_activity.pid = blocking_locks.pid
WHERE NOT blocked_locks.GRANTED;
```

### Check Running Queries
```sql
SELECT relation::regclass, * FROM pg_locks WHERE NOT GRANTED;
SELECT * FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE pid = <pid>;
```

### Kill Process
```sql
SELECT pg_terminate_backend(pid)
FROM pg_stat_activity
WHERE usename = '<username>';
```

---

## 7. Replication Lag

### Check if Primary or Replica
```sql
SELECT pg_is_in_recovery();  -- true = replica, false = primary
SELECT * FROM pg_stat_wal_receiver;
```

### On Primary Server
```bash
ps -ef | grep -i postgres | grep data
ls -a
. .dbname
psql / psql -U dbadmin
\x
```

### Check Replication Status
```sql
SELECT client_addr, usename, backend_start, write_lag, flush_lag, replay_lag, state, sync_state
FROM pg_stat_replication;
```

> **Note:** If state = streaming, replication is running.

---

## 8. Disk Consumption Percentage

### Check Disk Usage
```bash
df -kh
cd <largest_used_directory>
du -sh *
```

### Connect to Database
```bash
ps -ef | grep -i postgres | grep data
ls -a
. .dbname
psql / psql -U dbadmin
\c <database_name>
```

---

## 9. Check Table Size / Top Tables

### Connect to Database
```sql
\c <database_name>
```

### Top 10 Tables by Size
```sql
WITH RECURSIVE pg_inherit(inhrelid, inhparent) AS (
    SELECT inhrelid, inhparent FROM pg_inherits
    UNION
    SELECT child.inhrelid, parent.inhparent
    FROM pg_inherit child, pg_inherits parent
    WHERE child.inhparent = parent.inhrelid
),
pg_inherit_short AS (
    SELECT * FROM pg_inherit
    WHERE inhparent NOT IN (SELECT inhrelid FROM pg_inherit)
)
SELECT table_schema, TABLE_NAME, row_estimate,
       pg_size_pretty(total_bytes) AS total,
       pg_size_pretty(index_bytes) AS INDEX,
       pg_size_pretty(toast_bytes) AS toast,
       pg_size_pretty(table_bytes) AS TABLE
FROM (
    SELECT *, total_bytes - index_bytes - COALESCE(toast_bytes, 0) AS table_bytes
    FROM (
        SELECT c.oid, nspname AS table_schema, relname AS TABLE_NAME,
               SUM(c.reltuples) OVER (partition BY parent) AS row_estimate,
               SUM(pg_total_relation_size(c.oid)) OVER (partition BY parent) AS total_bytes,
               SUM(pg_indexes_size(c.oid)) OVER (partition BY parent) AS index_bytes,
               SUM(pg_total_relation_size(reltoastrelid)) OVER (partition BY parent) AS toast_bytes,
               parent
        FROM (
            SELECT pg_class.oid, reltuples, relname, relnamespace, pg_class.reltoastrelid,
                   COALESCE(inhparent, pg_class.oid) parent
            FROM pg_class LEFT JOIN pg_inherit_short ON inhrelid = oid
            WHERE relkind IN ('r', 'p')
        ) c
        LEFT JOIN pg_namespace n ON n.oid = c.relnamespace
    ) a
    WHERE oid = parent
) a
ORDER BY table_bytes DESC
LIMIT 10;
```

---

## 10. Slow Log

### Navigate to Logs
```bash
ps -ef | grep -i postgres | grep data
ls -a
. .dbname
cd $PGDATA/log
ls -lrth
```

### Count Slow Queries
```bash
cat pgdb-2022-06-03_*.log | grep -i duration | wc -l
cat pgdb-2022-06-03_*.log | grep -i error | wc -l
```

> Analyze queries taking above 3 seconds (duration). Perform `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` on slow queries.

---

## 11. Archive Check & Housekeeping

### Navigate to Archive
```bash
cd /backup_DB_rafmpdb01/backup_PPRAFM/archive
```

### Count Files
```bash
find . -type f -printf '%TY-%Tm-%Td-%TH\n' | sort | uniq -c  # per hour
find . -type f -printf '%TY-%Tm-%Td\n' | sort | uniq -c       # per day
find . -type f -printf '%TY-%Tm\n' | sort | uniq -c           # per month
du -sh .                                                       # active files
```

### Find Files by Time
```bash
find . -name '0000000*' -mmin +1400 | wc -l    # by minutes
find . -name '0000000*' -mtime +2 | wc -l      # by days
find . -newermt "2024-11-06 00:00:00" ! -newermt "2024-11-10 23:59:59" | wc -l
```

### Delete Old Files
```bash
find . -name '0000000*' -mmin +1400 -delete    # by minutes
find . -name '0000000*' -mtime +2 -delete      # by days
find . -newermt "2023-04-15 00:00:00" ! -newermt "2023-04-15 23:59:59" -delete
```

---

## 12. ACL (Access Control List)

### Reload Configuration
```sql
SELECT pg_reload_conf();
```

### Check pg_hba Rules
```sql
SELECT * FROM pg_hba_file_rules WHERE database = '{mlflow}';
SELECT * FROM pg_hba_file_rules WHERE user_name = '{pemuser}';
SELECT * FROM pg_hba_file_rules WHERE address = '10.251.38.112';
SHOW port;
\! date;
hostname -f;
```

### Example pg_hba Entry
```
host    postgres        efmuser         10.38.18.68/32          scram-sha-256
```
